_what: Every device surface Trillion ships, and how each one wears the one look (parts/ui + parts/screen-look over src/workspace/looks.json). A new platform (a watch, Windows, Android, glasses) is a row here, never a new design. draws says how the host gets the look: shared-parts hosts run the web parts themselves (a browser, the Chrome extension, a native window around a web view); compiled-look hosts cannot run them (a widget, a share sheet, a Live Activity, a complication) and read the look compiled into their own language by scripts/make-device-looks.mjs, one file per generated row. source_roots are the folders a host draws from: scripts/check-device-hosts.mjs refuses any line there that draws content with a platform's stock control (stock_controls, by the host's language), so a stock menu, alert, form or list cannot reach a person. A language with no stock_controls row and no emitter is a gap the check names, never a pass. A compiled-look host's first-launch look is src/workspace/looks.json start_with, the look every page and a new account start with (scripts/make-device-looks.mjs); once the account answers, every compiled-look host draws the look the person wears now (GET /looks/device, ios/Shared/WornLook.swift). `surfaces` names a theme for a part of a host whose ground the platform fixes whatever the person wears (the Dynamic Island is always black glass), so its words stay readable there; the worn look still gives it the accent and states. `look_literals` are, by language, the ways a line can decide a colour, a face or a theme itself instead of reading the look (scripts/check-device-hosts.mjs refuses them in every host's source, strings included); `look_files` are the only files that may, because they are where the look is read (the generated files are look files too).
